A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DTE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be aligned despite revisions and pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original DTE and multi-agent debate experiments, benchmark accuracies, ablations, and extensive supplementary results in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds MATH and GPQA Main comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: Although the DTE loop and RCR prompts remain, the specified training rule changes substantially. V1 uses raw rewards in its surrogate and explicitly mentions a value-network baseline; v2 specifies group-normalized advantages and training without a value network. This changes the documented objective and training components, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on competition-level MATH and graduate-level biology, physics, and chemistry questions from GPQA Main. This substantially extends difficulty and task coverage beyond the five retained arithmetic, school-science, and commonsense benchmarks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged: original models and RCR-MAD in Table 1, SFT and DPO in Table 3, and original MAD and Majority Vote@3 in Appendix F. The added benchmarks use the existing Table 1 comparison structure.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated learning rate from 2×10^-5 to 5×10^-6 and weight decay from 0.01 to 0.1, matching both versions' Appendix B; v2 Section 3.3 still retains the old values. This is a reported-setting revision, not evidence of reruns. New evaluations specify 5,000 MATH test problems and 448 test-only GPQA Main questions.

E4.justification: The RCR, agent-count/diversity, optimization-objective, data-selection, training-duration, temperature, and iterative-evolution analyses are retained. Appendices D–F contain the same analyses and results after alignment. The two added benchmark comparisons introduce no corresponding new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's new reward standard deviation is part of GRPO training, not uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds original-model, MAD, and DTE scores for all six models on MATH and GPQA Main. Reported DTE gains over their respective base models range from 2.74–7.12 points on MATH and 0.68–6.64 on GPQA. These are new benchmark results; the retained Table 1 entries and Appendix D–F results are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.3 substantially reformulates the mathematics: it defines group reward statistics and normalized advantages, introduces a token-averaged clipped loss and per-token KL expression, and supplies a gradient expression. This goes beyond equivalent notation or explanation of v1's shorter sequence-level surrogate. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The core claims remain ground-truth-free self-evolution through debate traces, improved debate through RCR, efficient single-model inference, and cross-domain reasoning gains. The headline 8.92% and 5.8% claims remain. Updating the abstract's benchmark count from five to seven expands supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of group normalization across reward scales, memory savings from eliminating the value network, and the distinct roles of clipping and KL regularization. Interpretations of the empirical results and the limitations concerning forgetting, trace quality, open-ended tasks, and training costs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds project/repository access information for code and models, group size G=8, explicit appendix reward weights, hyperparameter-selection information, runtime/GPU-hour estimates, and licensing details. It removes v1's 2048-token sequence and 512/1536-token prompt/completion limits. Resource status is inconsistently documented: the abstract says publicly available, while Appendix B promises future release.

R1.justification: V2 adds MATH, GPQA, BeyondBench, and LLMThinkBench references and removes the Hu, Kotha, and Luo references. Several other changes merely update publication metadata for retained works. The related-work narrative and positioning of DTE against prior approaches remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The method section is substantially rewritten and reorganized into four subsections separating preliminary analysis, RCR, GRPO training, and evolution. Appendices A and B are also rewritten into clearer topical descriptions. Additional edits affect author information, acknowledgements, and the new AI-assistance statement; most results prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from three to five benchmark groups and compresses its text from approximately 8-point to 5-point type. Table 5 gains dataset rows, algorithms expand and move, and prompt boxes reflow. Figures 1–6 and the remaining result-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable harder-benchmark evidence and more training, compute, and access documentation. However, unlike v1's maximized surrogate, its new loss negates the clipped reward term while retaining a negative KL term, conflicting with the stated penalty under minimization. Optimizer and reward-description inconsistencies persist, and sequence-length limits disappear. These benefits and technical/documentation regressions leave the net quality direction uncertain.
